# SOUL civilization gaps and founder camp roadmap

SOUL now supports a separate founder camp with no permanent homes, assigned occupations or authored daily routines. This page distinguishes the delivered browser implementation from the learning and long-duration civilization evidence still needed. Existing furnished villages remain supported.

## Balance basic abilities with learned choices

Provide working bodies, navigation, reach checks, carrying, interaction and resource owners. Let each person choose among currently available proposals and learn from their own consequences. An adult does not need to rediscover limb control before gathering food or experimenting with a tool.

| Layer | Delivered foundation | Learning or evidence still needed |
|---|---|---|
| Body and world | Stable identities, one world/two views, actual routes, collision, carrying, placement and owner receipts | Broader motor skills, deliberate route efficiency and perceptual transfer |
| Personal behavior | Empty initial procedure memory; exploration, repeated outcome statistics, revisions, private RNG and delivered teaching | Reliable multi-step planning and transfer across novel contexts |
| Resources | Finite sites, water/food, tool wear/custody, replacement tools, repair, storage, exchanges and accepted deliveries | Regrowth, farming, refining, weather and sustainable production |
| Homes | Resident proposals, bounded dimensions, one/two floors, private beds, shared cooking/living space, material-backed stages and invitations | Demonstrated learned design quality, broader building programs and settlement planning |
| Society | Mutual relationships/families, care, fighting, theft, local commitments, communities and ballots | Unforced durable division of labor, successful family care and several generations of survival |
| Neural learning | WebGPU candidate training, reviewed generic decision records, held-out gates and separate serving checkpoint | A competent observation-dependent civilization policy and broad conversation |

The engine decides whether an action is possible and records its actual result. Personal outcome learning can value actor benefit, harm, relationships and commitments differently. A completed theft or fight is not automatically labelled desirable or approved for shared training.

Sources: `agi/soul/SoulFounder.js`, `SoulDiscovery.js`, `SoulEconomy.js`, `SoulShelter.js`, `SoulSociety.js`, `SoulWorld.js`.

## Delivered scenarios and workflow

A fresh app opens paused with 100 founders and no model allocation. Project setup offers new populations of 2, 8, 32 or 100. Eight is a useful engineering test size, not a research-derived optimum. Creating a camp first archives the prior complete project. **Exports → Download previous project** makes that archive available for import. Existing village imports preserve their homes, authored daily lessons and utility controller.

The actual starter kit contains two shared stone axes, two shared picks, a workbench, a basket and loose bedroll per person, and two food units/two litres of water per person in a shared depot. It does not currently include crops, a farm, a saw, a fire/weather system or a renewable forest. Hand gathering branches, loose stone and fibre can supply a replacement axe without requiring an existing axe. A one-axe scarcity scenario is still a future separately balanced experiment.

Founder needs and navigation work without a home. Resource observations require personal visibility; remembered stock can become stale. Accepted delivery requests communicate a meeting location rather than granting access to the requester's hidden live position. A child starts with fresh personal discovery, including when the family has no permanent house.

**Play society** uses `personal-outcomes-v1`. Optional serving-model participation adds a small WebGPU-scored shortlist and labels the combined controller explicitly. It does not start training. Available proposals are bounded by kind and rotated targets so a crowded scene cannot permanently displace shelter actions with earlier social/resource options. The authors still define possible actions, recipes, need effects and proposal affordances; this is not independent invention of arbitrary programs.

Sources: `webgpu-os/apps/soul/SoulApp.js`, `SoulStorage.js`, `RealmForgeWorld.js`; `agi/soul/SoulFounder.js`, `SoulEconomy.js`, `SoulLife.js`, `SoulSociety.js`.

## Shared literature and personally delivered learning

The default library implements a scarce starting collection: 38 titles and 42 physical copies on two shared founder shelves or eight selected household shelves in the 100-person furnished village. It retains the supplied plan’s 100 fictional example passages and adds short complete original first editions, including 100 actual microstories. Titles are not empty promises, and fictional diaries, registers and chronicles never become invented resident histories.

Reading is an actual object/task effect with copy, edition, receipt and tick provenance. Only readers acquire the text. Local teaching can carry that passage onward with a bounded delivery lineage; it grants no fabricated practice or neural competence. The operator catalogue, personal records and physical copies are distinct projections. Durable drafts and publishing preserve old reading editions while updating existing copies, without creating a copy per person or approving a shared training record.

Following evidence still needed: whether residents voluntarily finish useful books, retain their content, relate passages to observed situations, teach accurately, and improve held-out decisions after reviewed WebGPU training. Semantic text access currently bypasses optical page perception; OCR, learned reading comprehension, physical pages, spontaneous authorship and resident printing/copy production remain separate work. The 256-passage personal limit and 16-link teaching limit are explicit engineering bounds.

Sources: `agi/soul/SoulLibrary.js`, `SoulDefaultBooks.js`; `webgpu-os/apps/soul/SoulLibraryGeometry.js`, `SoulApp.js`; `tests/soul/library.test.js`.

## Personal procedures and truthful outcomes

Each individual retains at most 64 single-action procedures, 32 independent sequence variants and 128 recent episodes. Saved personal RNG makes the next exploration choice reproducible without other people's choices advancing that RNG. Physical-action contexts in `soul.skill-conditions.v2` include relevant needs, inputs, capacity, target state and required tools. Unrelated goods and need bands no longer fragment those procedures. Other actions retain conservative full contexts; the exact-context baseline preserves its original behavior.

The `terminal-dependencies-v2` bank stores each sequence's steps, starting conditions, independent receipt traces, attempts, successes, failures and observed return. A new prefix cannot replace another variant's support. Sequences contain at most four steps and project relevant later needs into their starting conditions. A variant becomes executable after two personal completions, a completion fraction of at least 60% and positive mean observed return. Rejection or interruption contributes the actual partial return and failure evidence. These thresholds are engineering policy settings, not calibrated success probabilities.

Dependency extraction starts at the terminal owner effect and follows only its material or tool prerequisites. The production owners record actual `consumedInputs` for crafting, repair, delivery and shelter work. The learner checks inventory deltas and accounts for intervening spending; tool prerequisites require acquisition, crafting or repair followed by measured wear. A shared commitment, passive energy recovery or nearby timestamps cannot establish a chain. Need, material and tool effects retain their measured values, including negative intermediate effort; there is no fabricated completion bonus.

Locally delivered teaching copies a procedure or relevant sequence variant with explicit teacher provenance. Newly taught procedures and variants start with zero recipient trials, outcomes and receipt evidence. Existing personal knowledge stays intact when a new sequence arrives. A bounded teacher prior can influence a single-action choice. An applicable taught sequence may now enter explicitly labelled practice at most twice, with an eight-personal-decision cooldown between starts. The recipient must choose a currently available first action, and every later step still requires an available owner action and its real result. Practice has separate start, completion and failure counters; ordinary learned execution still requires two verified personal traces and the existing return/completion thresholds. The controller uses only the individual's supplied observations and own state. The operator dashboard remains a separate read-only projection.

Admission, work completion and cancellation have distinct receipts. Rest cannot run productive work concurrently. Work can pause, survive restore and resume under its original receipt; cancelled work cannot become a success. Manual conflicting actions cannot overwrite a pending personal action. Personal travel does not send an authored greeting and does not create a duplicate Founder-owned shared lesson. Restore validates active sequence references, receipt counts, step identities and receipt chronology, alongside pending evidence and the experience outbox. Legacy sequence records remain historical; active legacy executions enter recovery when the revised semantic controller initializes its sequence bank.

Immediate procedure updates are episodic/statistical JavaScript state. Neural weight updates require reviewed datasets and explicit browser training. All neural forward passes, loss, backpropagation and optimizer updates use WebGPU.

Sources: `agi/soul/SoulDiscovery.js`, `SoulFounder.js`, `SoulEconomy.js`, `SoulShelter.js`, `SoulLife.js`, `SoulWorldState.js`, `Curriculum.js`, `SoulRuntime.js`; `tests/soul/discovery.test.js`, `founder-skills.test.js`, `founder-interruption.test.js`.

## Resources, construction and placement

### Next physical interaction: doors

The 1 October audit confirms that residents cannot yet open or close doors. SOUL's furnished cottage compiles a fixed open leaf into its shell groups and does not request RealmForge's optional mechanism generation. Founder shelters currently have open doorways. General rendering and ForgeSource compilation do not supply an executable action for every object.

Build the connection in this order:

1. Add a versioned mechanism-enabled SOUL template with separately bound leaf, handle, hinge and frame identities; preserve legacy fixed-open projects.
2. Expose only personally observed interaction points and state. Admit approach/reservation through the existing actor-task owner, including reach and occupancy checks.
3. Request opening or closing through `RealmForgeConstructionPresetPhysics.setArticulationOpening`; retain its locked, busy and blocked outcomes. Use measured articulation state as completion evidence.
4. Publish the same leaf pose and collision state to both views and invalidate affected navigation. Refuse travel through an unavailable or still-closed passage.
5. Save mechanism state and pending task identity. Test interrupted opening, competing people, obstruction, locked doors, restore and stale observation without duplicate effects.
6. Record storylets from those actual outcomes, then teach and evaluate choosing the interaction. Expected success is a hypothesis until observed.

Reuse `RealmForgeActorUseRuntime` for its supported approach/use contracts rather than duplicating them. Its current 16-actor bound and the mechanism runtime's serialized active request require explicit scheduling and population tests. Extend the same pattern to storage lids, taps, switches and appliances only when their physical owners are connected. Storylet prose and dictionary definitions cannot operate missing mechanisms.

Sources: `webgpu-os/apps/soul/SoulAssets.js`, `SoulVillage.js`; `agi/soul/SoulFounderActions.js`, `SoulShelter.js`; `webgpu-os/apps/realmforge/construction/runtime/RealmForgeConstructionPresetPhysics.js`, `interactions/RealmForgeActorUseRuntime.js`, `interactions/RealmForgeObjectActionRuntime.js`.

The founder economy owns finite spatial sites, distinct tool ownership/custody, carrying capacity, observed workstations, reservations, work progress and conservation ledgers. Gathering, chopping and mining require actual reach and elapsed work. Recipes and repairs reserve real inputs; outputs appear only when completed and able to fit. Borrowing, tool theft, local exchange and accepted delivery use the same committed owner paths. Accepted construction work exposes its next material deficit, which can inform available requests and gathering without assigning a fixed job sequence.

Shared `AIEconomy` station, capacity and production-destination defects identified during the audit were corrected and covered by regression tests. SOUL still owns its separate physical production transactions; a recipe helper alone does not supply durability, hauling, ownership or exactly-once world effects.

Shelter designs currently validate 4–12 m width, 6–12 m depth, one/two floors, one to three sleeping rooms per floor and a private sleeping room per resident. Staged wood/stone/fibre costs install the actual generated pieces. Two-floor fixtures exercise physical stairs, upper-floor beds and mid-stair restoration. These bounded assemblies are compiled through RealmForge; they do not modify RealmForge's general text resolver to accept arbitrary apartment or condominium programs.

Founder shelter stage/part counts depend on the proposed design. The legacy furnished village's 12-stage, 2,075-piece cottage and prepared stock for 28 expansions remain a separate system. Founders begin without that prefab stock or those houses.

Movable bedrolls and supported furniture preserve IDs, geometry, interaction anchors and restored placement. Structural pieces remain construction-owned. A support cannot be moved while another object depends on it; the dependent object must be removed first. Cooking fixtures and water inventory do not imply plumbing, utilities or a simulated fire system.

Sources: `agi/soul/SoulEconomy.js`, `SoulShelter.js`, `SoulPlacement.js`, `SoulNavigation.js`; `engine/sim/ai/AIEconomy.js`; `webgpu-os/apps/soul/SoulHousing.js`, `SoulVillage.js`; `tests/soul/economy.test.js`, `shelter-world.test.js`.

## Live civilization reporting

The operator dashboard has a searchable/sortable population table and a selected-person panel. It separates current activity, accepted work and role, and reports health, energy, hunger, thirst, inventory, tool custody/condition, family, relationships and personal procedures. Resource tables distinguish carried, stored, reserved and natural quantities. Construction, local offers and retained events remain inspectable.

Rendering coalesces committed updates and retains keyed rows, selection and focus. Runtime reporting exposes nested training metrics and labels the decision budget per tick. Model allocation is not total GPU VRAM. The population benchmark uses only cohort sizes that exist in the project; unavailable/busy people are counted separately, and founder replays do not inject authored routines.

The operator now retains bounded 10-second samples, per-person deprivation and outcome counts, resource production/consumption and 600-second work windows. Historical food runway, mortality and migration still require additional models and measurements. Current incapacitation is temporary, so endpoint able counts must not be called survival or mortality rates. A settlement total also does not prove that every individual has access to its stock.

Strict useful chains use `soul.outcome-chain.v2` within `soul.metrics.v2`. Every controller receives the same terminal dependency test and positive-return requirement. Migration preserves v1 counts and samples as `legacyHeuristicChains`, resets strict chain totals and records their new `strictChainsSince` time. Learned execution completions remain a separate diagnostic. Earlier heuristic totals cannot support a strict-chain acceptance claim, and summed deprivation counts overlapping need conditions separately.

Sources: `agi/soul/SoulMetrics.js`; `webgpu-os/apps/soul/SoulDashboard.js`, `SoulApp.js`, `SoulMeasurements.js`; `tests/soul/founder-app.test.js`, `dashboard.test.js`, `founder-trials.test.js`.

## Dictionary, storylets and neural gaps

The dictionary and lexicons reduce manual source writing. They supply terms, definitions, relationships and pronunciation evidence. The model still needs examples connecting terms to observations and consequences. A definition of an axe does not establish that the model recognizes a visible axe or understands its availability and ownership.

Storylets and personal outcomes create drafts. Generic decision records preserve pre-action evidence and exact available proposals behind short labels. The compiler checks those identities, keeps source/episode groups together and rejects altered targets. Candidate training never automatically replaces serving weights. Shared training also needs future eligibility rules and tests for private facts; personal memory separation alone does not prove that a model trained on approved personal content cannot reveal it.

The measured new decision fixture has 37 training, 5 validation and 3 test rows. After two GPU updates it scored **20% validation accuracy**, also **20% with missing evidence**. Its promotion gate failed and serving weights remained unchanged. This verifies the workflow and rejects an inadequate candidate; it does not demonstrate an effective neural civilization policy.

The explicit v3 controlled model now passes 120/120 validation choices and 47/48 untouched test choices for needs, resource availability and tool condition, with 50% missing-evidence accuracy and 60/60 opposed-evidence validation pairs. It was trained from browser random weights for 150 updates. The [workflow guide](soul.md#grounded-v3-model-26-september-2026) records numerical checks, artifact paths and limits. This result does not establish a complete civilization policy.

The earlier six-home-command model remains a separate result: 48/48 additional fixed-goal choices, 2/6 untrained paraphrases and 6/6 fixed-goal choices with missing observations. The legacy models do not establish dependence on perceived evidence. The v3 fixture establishes dependence on structured needs, stock and tool evidence, while live visual perception remains unverified. Legacy v2 live inputs retain bounded spatial features and compressed memory. Explicit v3 adds 64 personal features and 96 features per considered action, including own needs/goods/tools, accepted commitments and permitted target evidence. Personal camera crops/OCR are not yet feeding the normal live decision loop; imported images use an 8 by 8 grayscale representation.

The current paired-view alignment objective pulls matching representations together. Distinguishing nonmatching scenes, explicit object identity/containment and observer-relative relation targets are still needed. Add paired versus single-view baselines, unseen viewpoints, occlusion and contradictory evidence. The 192-byte-token context bounds current shortlists; richer context or architecture requires a new explicit measured version.

Sources: `agi/soul/Curriculum.js`, `SoulRuntime.js`, `SoulWorld.js`, `Observation.js`, `PaiGPU.js`, `PaiProfile.js`; `tests/soul/latest-discovery-learning-result.json`, `latest-action-transfer-result.json`; `artifacts/soul-goal-learning-2026-09-26/verification.json`.

### Research that informs this recommendation

| Primary source | Relevant finding | Application to SOUL |
|---|---|---|
| [Voyager, Wang et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.16291) | Combines an automatic curriculum, reusable executable skills and feedback from execution. It uses an existing large model without weight updates. | Reuse verified skills and choose attainable new challenges. This does not demonstrate equivalent ability in SOUL's tiny browser model. |
| [Video PreTraining, Baker et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2206.11795) | A learned behavioral prior helped Minecraft agents reach long action sequences that were difficult from scratch. | Provide basic action competence and demonstrations before asking for complex independent production. Its training scale is not an 8 GB browser budget. |
| [Generative Agents, Park et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.03442) | Evaluates observation, retrieved memory, reflection and planning in a 25-agent social sandbox using a large language model. | Test personal memory and communicated plans as separate components. Believable interactions do not establish a conserved, self-sufficient economy. |
| [Crafter, Hafner](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.06780) | Uses survival, resource discovery and crafting achievements to evaluate a range of capabilities. | Measure concrete milestones and transfer instead of using fluent dialogue or training loss as the civilization score. |
| [Melting Pot 2.0, Agapiou et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2211.13746) | Evaluates agents with unfamiliar social partners and mixed cooperative/competitive incentives. | Test sharing, scarcity and conflict with varied partners and seeds, including alternatives to cooperation. |
| [Accumulating Real and Synthetic Data, Gerstgrasser et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.01413) | In its studied settings, retaining original data alongside accumulated synthetic data avoided collapse seen with replacement. | Preserve reviewed originals and validate continued training. This supports a data-retention strategy, not a guarantee for SOUL. |

These are design inferences from the cited research. Neural inference, loss, backpropagation and optimizer updates in SOUL remain WebGPU work. JavaScript continues to own preparation, simulation, scheduling and files. The immediate goal is a measured skill and decision model; broad conversation and social competence need their own data and evaluation.

## Verification and remaining acceptance gates

Real Chrome/Blackwell checks establish bounded capabilities, not an autonomous civilization success claim:

- The latest personal outcome fixture prefers a repeatedly useful action in **184 of 200** subsequent choices, preserves individual RNG and private evidence, revises failures and requires delivered teaching. Source: `tests/soul/latest-discovery-result.json`.
- The native app mounts 100 founders with 3,371 rendered pieces and 83 draws in the measured initial scene. It verifies both OS-owned views, lazy model allocation, archiving 100 people before creating an eight-person camp, actual GPU proposal scoring, project restoration and cleanup.
- Founder interruption tests cover rest/work exclusivity, mid-work restore, failed-write rollback, original receipt continuation, cancellation and corrupt pending evidence rejection.
- Family capability tests use explicit relationship and due-date fixtures. They verify mutual acceptance, a no-home child with fresh discovery, conserved care/theft effects, observed fighting consequences and teaching boundaries. They do not claim spontaneous multi-generation success.
- Shelter capability fixtures physically build and traverse two floors, restore partway through stairs, move household furniture and reject conflicting placement. They do not prove that the personal or neural controller independently chose and completed that whole sequence.

Reports are retained under `tests/soul/latest-*-result.json`. Reproduce founder-specific checks with:

```powershell
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page discovery.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page discovery-learning.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page founder.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page founder-family.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page founder-interruption.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page economy.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page shelter-world.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page custody.html
python tests/soul/run_gpu.py --page founder-scale.html
python tests/soul/run_founder_app.py
```

| Next gate | Required evidence |
|---|---|
| Useful unforced discovery | Several seeds; obtaining food/water, borrowing or replacing a tool, material delivery, shelter completion and recovery without forced successful decisions |
| Learned decision quality | Observation-changing targets, unfamiliar wording/partners, exhausted or hidden sites, broken tools, stale memories, intervention and missing-evidence comparisons |
| Sustainable economy | Explicit renewable resources or finite-horizon limits, work/need balancing, no duplicated stock, distributions of access and failed deliveries |
| Social development | Long-duration family care, conflict consequences, voluntary work, rules and leadership; report failures and severe unmet needs alongside averages |
| Browser scale and retention | Improve the measured founder cohorts through 100 (v3 measured 2.23 proposals/second with both views in the latest isolated cohort run); extend training contention and device-loss tests, bounded history and held-out retention after continued training |
| Broader modalities | Live OCR/camera grounding, paired/single-view comparisons, supervised speech paths and multimodal contradiction handling |

Keep the legacy utility controller identified as a baseline. Comparisons must use matched supplies, permitted observations and scene seeds; comparing a stocked furnished village with a finite founder camp cannot isolate the policy effect. Retain reviewed originals when adding generated experience, and measure what the candidate forgets.

Movement and work retain metres and simulation seconds. New founder projects declare a saved 600-second day and corresponding daily need rates; older saves without that policy retain their original rates. Reports include the policy so survival horizons, tool use and demographic time are not silently conflated. Finite food and water mean the current camp cannot demonstrate indefinite sustainability without a replenishment or external-supply model.

## Learning slice: implementation and acceptance

Research review and implementation: 26 September 2026. The six implementation areas below now have browser code and verification paths. Their empirical acceptance gates remain separate claims: controlled skill or model tests do not establish unforced civilization competence. The existing 100-person project stays supported; eight-person worlds make the independent trials inspectable.

Focused tests now demonstrate transfer to another object or location and recovery through selected interruptions; unforced behavior remains a separate acceptance gate. Roles, schedules and house assignments remain unassigned. Basic movement and physical interactions remain provided capabilities.

### Gaps identified before this implementation

| Priority | Gap observed in the preceding audit | Implemented response |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Native collection constructs `[selected, ...alternatives]`, then the compiler labels options by position. Every retained native choice therefore targets `a0`. The synthetic fixture rotates selected targets and misses this shortcut. | Counterbalance candidate order while preserving action identity, capture the actual available shortlist independently of the winner, and evaluate a constant-first baseline. Preserve affected records and require fresh, valid collection before decision training. |
| 1 | `SoulDiscovery.conditions` includes exact inventory, target and visible object IDs; `choose` requires an exact context/action match. Stored `steps` do not execute a skill. | Separate reusable skill conditions from a particular execution's IDs. Bind observed targets at execution, check each step and retain actual identities in personal memory and receipts. |
| 2 | Live `SoulWorld.modelInput` supplies 16 spatial values, including offsets/portability for only the first three visible objects, and a 32-value byte summary of memory. It has no explicit need, tool condition or commitment fields. | Version the observation and candidate encoders. Include own needs, carried resources, usable tools, accepted commitments and permitted object features. Evidence age remains a future feature. Bind each candidate to its observed target. |
| 3 | Travel for a selected resource action finishes before productive work. Immediate rewards credit a single recorded attempt. | Represent approach, interaction and verified outcome as separate phases of one bounded attempt. Arrival is a completed travel phase; resource acquisition requires the owner's productive receipt. Credit earlier steps when their actual later consequence arrives. |
| 4 | Existing passing fixtures mostly establish capabilities. The generic neural fixture has only five validation rows and failed its promotion gate. | Add repeatable autonomous rollouts, larger grouped decision evaluations, intervention tests and matched controller comparisons. |
| 5 | Water/food are finite, while needs, work and demographic clocks use different scales. | Declare and test a finite survival horizon and coherent rates before interpreting civilization longevity. Introduce explicit renewable production in a following slice. |
| 6 | Candidate likelihood scoring runs a full model forward pass and readback for each option. World transactions also clone/validate state. | Profile GPU compute, readbacks, simulation, persistence and rendering separately. Then share candidate computation and batch ready decisions where the measurements justify it. |

Sources: `agi/soul/SoulDiscovery.js:57`, `SoulDiscovery.js:89`, `SoulDiscovery.js:128`, `SoulFounder.js:84`, `SoulFounder.js:94`, `SoulFounder.js:135`, `SoulWorld.js:144`, `SoulRuntime.js:41`, `Curriculum.js:16`, `Curriculum.js:78`; `webgpu-os/apps/soul/SoulApp.js:60`; `tests/soul/discovery-learning.test.js:10`, `latest-discovery-learning-result.json`.

### Delivered implementation order

1. **[MODIFY] Repair decision collection and establish the baseline.** Counterbalance candidate order with stable action bindings and a separate saved collection RNG. Capture the actual considered alternatives. Keep originals; require revalidation of affected training records. Extend `SoulMeasurements` with fixed seeds, a declared time policy/supplies/horizon and per-person outcomes. Capture isolated performance; compare render-optional trials with rendered replays using the same owners.
2. **[MODIFY] Generalize personal procedures.** Extend `SoulDiscovery` with typed target bindings and relevant preconditions, preserving personal provenance and confidence. Reusing an axe skill must not require the same axe ID. Ownership, containment, visibility and meaningful individual relationships remain checked.
3. **[MODIFY] Execute bounded, interruptible skills.** Extend Founder/actor task execution with phase receipts, completion conditions, cancellation, recovery and delayed outcome attribution. Bound attempts, loops and work budgets. At each step, re-observe and revalidate through the existing owner.
4. **[MODIFY] Ground the small neural policy.** Extend the shared SOUL core with versioned observation/candidate features and a candidate scoring head. Retain the Pai language path. Keep all neural forward/loss/backward/optimizer work on WebGPU and verify gradients into every enabled encoder. Reuse GPU/storage ownership and checkpoint packaging.
5. **[MODIFY] Compile useful experience and verify transfer.** Extend Curriculum with whole-attempt grouping, failed attempts, interrupted work, alternative outcomes, stale evidence and contradictory observations. A selected action is a behavior observation, not an expert target; use reviewed success criteria or outcome/value targets to learn quality. Review drafts explicitly; retain dictionary/OCR originals. Train the candidate, run held-out evaluation and use the existing promotion gate.
6. **[MODIFY] Explain measured behavior in the dashboard.** Show the current self-selected objective, skill step, target, observed evidence, confidence, last result and recovery. Derive provisional job labels from completed work over a rolling window; show “unestablished” until evidence exists. Add food/water access, deprivation, production/consumption and unfinished-work trends.

The browser now exposes both trial paths, explicit source assessment, the v3 architecture and outcome/skill dashboards. Export/restore retains the controller, RNG, active skill, measurement window and separate candidate/serving models. Exact-context and random baselines remain available in isolated measurements. New policy versions still require measured validation before promotion.

An example chain is personally obtaining a tool, approaching an observed tree, chopping, carrying material and using it in accepted work. This is an evaluation target and a possible discovered behavior, not a timetable assigned to every founder. Goals can arise from personal needs, curiosity or voluntarily accepted commitments. The operator does not supply occupation quotas.

### Acceptance gates and interpretation

These numbers are initial engineering targets. Set them before evaluation and report failures; they are not published research thresholds.

- **Transfer:** at least 100 held-out skill trials across 20 scene seeds, covering food/water access, tool acquisition or replacement, and material delivery to accepted construction. Target at least 80% verified completion overall and in every task, within eight choices and 180 simulation seconds. Report first-choice correctness separately and account for tasks sharing a seed. Separate these focused goal-conditioned trials from free-choice society trials.
- **Independent behavior:** run eight founders on the same 20 held-out seeds for a declared, resource-feasible horizon with no forced successful choices, assigned jobs or supplied plans. Report per-person minimum health, ever-incapacitated state and deprivation plus voluntarily completed milestones, including failures. Compare random legal choices, current personal outcomes and the new controller with matched evidence and supplies. The implemented gate requires the upper bound of the paired deprivation-difference interval to be at most zero and the lower bound of the useful-chain improvement interval to exceed zero against each baseline. Count useful chains from the same actual owner receipts for every controller. Learned-chain execution remains diagnostic. Summed deprivation can count overlapping need conditions; endpoint health is not a mortality measure.
- **Adaptation:** exhaust a known resource, break a tool, move an item, interrupt work and obstruct an approach. Target at least 80% recovery in cases with an observable feasible alternative; impossible cases must terminate or change objective within the declared attempt budget.
- **Grounding:** use matched cases whose correct choice changes when needs, ownership, stock or tool condition change. Report full-evidence, missing-evidence and shuffled-evidence results with chance/majority/constant-first baselines. Test the native collection path and target-position coverage. Renaming irrelevant IDs and permuting object/candidate order must preserve the selected semantic action for deterministic inference.
- **Integrity:** no duplicated goods or effects, no access to hidden stocks or another Soul's private memory, no arrival labelled as productive completion, and no interrupted skill silently restarted as a new success after restore.
- **Browser budget:** report p50/p95 decision latency, completed decisions per second, queue age/depth, frame time, allocated model bytes and commit time at 8/32/100. Set a scheduling budget from the isolated baseline; the queue must remain bounded at the declared supported cadence. Earlier 63.21-second/100-decision evidence included development contention and is not an isolated benchmark.
- **Learning continuity:** export/import reproduces the next update within the declared FP32 tolerance. Promotion must preserve old skill evaluations and improve the held-out new skill set. A lower training loss alone does not pass.

### What the additional research changes

| Primary source | Evidence and limitation | SOUL recommendation |
|---|---|---|
| [SIMA 2, December 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.04797) | Uses a Gemini foundation model; its self-improvement loop uses Gemini to generate tasks and rewards. | Borrow the curriculum/feedback structure. In SOUL, engine receipts and observed consequences provide grounded feedback; storylet text alone cannot verify success. The paper does not establish tiny-model browser feasibility. |
| [DreamerV3](https://arxiv.org/abs/2301.04104) and [Dreamer 4](https://danijar.com/project/dreamer4/) | Study learning behavior through predicted futures; Dreamer 4 learns long Minecraft behavior from offline data. | Add measured outcome prediction and delayed credit incrementally. SOUL already owns an executable engine, so a learned video world simulator is a later research option with its own cost/accuracy gate. |
| [Craftax](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.16801) | Shows the importance of environment throughput for open-ended learning; its implementation uses JAX. | Reuse the browser world owners in render-optional trials and measure actual throughput. Its reported speed does not transfer to WebGPU by assumption. |
| [Set Transformer](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v97/lee19d.html) | Studies learning interactions over sets without relying on arbitrary input order. | Give observed objects and action candidates semantic feature bindings and test permutation behavior. Start with the smallest suitable set encoder; an exact architecture port is optional. |
| [Project Sid](https://arxiv.org/html/2411.00114v1) | Studies specialization and institutions, but reports limitations in spatial skills and drives. Its foundation models bring existing human knowledge and its authors do not claim de novo institutional invention. | Measure actual work, access, cooperation and adaptation. A generated job title or constitution is insufficient evidence of a functioning civilization. |

These applications are engineering inferences from the sources, not results measured in SOUL. The earlier Voyager evidence supports reusable executable skills; the data-accumulation study supports retaining original data during continued training without guaranteeing that generated records are correct.

### Group organization and coordination research

Research review: 26 September 2026. SOUL needs voluntary membership and explicit shared commitments above its existing physical action owners. A formation is a spatial arrangement, not evidence of a learned strategy. These sources inform the implementation; the applications below are engineering choices for SOUL.

| Primary source | Relevant mechanism | Application to SOUL |
|---|---|---|
| [Craig Reynolds, Steering Behaviors for Autonomous Characters](https://www.red3d.com/cwr/steer/gdc99/) | Separates action selection, steering and locomotion, and combines local movement behaviors. | Keep personal choices above formation destinations and existing collision-checked navigation. Reuse the engine's formation geometry without installing a second movement simulator. |
| [Milind Tambe, Towards Flexible Teamwork](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/9709101) | Shared commitments, communication and recovery address incomplete views and team failures. | Require delivered invitations and individual acceptance. Record departures, obstruction, failures and changed plans explicitly; membership does not disclose hidden positions or inventories. |
| [0 A.D. formation component](https://docs.wildfiregames.com/entity-docs/r28/components/formation/) | Documents shapes, footprint spacing and formation movement constrained by members. | Use bounded, deterministic assignments and test all accepted members. An absent member cannot count as having arrived. Coordinated pace and corridor reformation need separate measured movement capabilities. |
| [Epic Smart Objects overview](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/smart-objects-in-unreal-engine---overview) | Separates object availability and claims from execution and claim release. | Keep resources and construction reservations with their existing owners. Withdrawal must settle the actual pending work and release unused reservations without duplicating goods. |
| [Project Sid](https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.00114) | Studies cooperation and institutions using agents with substantial prior foundation-model knowledge. | Measure actual voluntary collaboration, distribution and recovery. Names, charters and job labels alone cannot establish civilization competence or tiny-model learning. |

Delivered and verified on 29 September 2026: group, clan, guild, company, gang and party ownership, mutual friendships, overlapping membership, local invitations, majority nomination and independent coordinator acceptance. Kinds express chosen purpose; they do not grant free goods, force crime, automatically recruit children or assign a person's daily routine. Membership and participation in a particular plan remain separate decisions. Protected collective property, currency, contracts enforced by institutions and ranged combat require further economy and combat owners.

The eleven plan kinds derive from permitted physical actions and currently observed targets. Saved personal decisions rotate offered formation alternatives across all seven shapes. Current personal plan disclosures include the participant's own assignment and revision. A stale disclosure cannot drive revised work until the update is delivered. Busy participants have continue/withdraw choices. Pending work is retired through the original economy, shelter or movement owner; lifecycle receipts never grant productive progress.

Fresh Chrome checks pass 18 organization groups, 20 group-plan groups, seven real-world integration groups, three protocol groups and ten dashboard groups. These fixtures verify mutual consent, measured navigation, approach-to-gather continuation, conserved production, cancellation, corruption rejection, failed-write rollback and isolation of an actor with an uncertain task effect. They do not demonstrate that the small model has learned strategy or that free-choice residents reliably build useful institutions. Sources: `tests/soul/latest-organizations-result.json`, `latest-group-plans-result.json`, `latest-group-world-result.json`, `latest-group-protocol-result.json`, `latest-dashboard-result.json`.

The current `pai-joint-v3` personal/candidate encoding does not represent group commitments, disclosed rosters or tactical evidence. New group choices retain exact proposal references and the personally disclosed context. GPU scoring and useful-choice group training refuse those unsupported inputs explicitly; observed factual outcomes can be reviewed as text. Population scoring reports excluded group choices. Neural choice training requires a separately versioned group input contract and held-out evaluation. Formation and membership tests establish available capabilities; autonomous selection and learned strategy require free-choice trials with unfamiliar partners and interrupted communication.

### Following slices

#### RealmForge and streamed worlds

The first renderer optimization is implemented. Atomic sparse matrix updates upload only affected instance batches. A transform-only SOUL source revision preserves meshes, materials and stable picking after conservative layout validation. Actual navigation with eight founders, a held axe and 2,048 static pieces uses 11,088 instance bytes per view per tick instead of 205,548, about an 18.5-fold reduction. A one-instance change among 16,384 static instances uses 84 bytes instead of 1,376,340. These are GPU upload counts, not isolated FPS or infinite-world evidence. A furnished 31,331-node village, home cutaway, occupant movement and overview restore pass actual GPU checks.

Two correctness fixes accompanied that measurement. The existing compact plumbing fallback now recognizes upstream structured room-fit errors while preserving required fixtures and clearances. Hierarchical coordinates no longer truncate sectors through signed 32-bit conversion; validated standard and BigInt carries normalize without distance-dependent loops. Large address tests do not establish a fully integrated enormous world.

The static presentation-region slice is implemented separately from gameplay. `SoulPresentationRegions` reuses Engine `ChunkStreaming` scheduling and keeps a versioned catalog of exact sector/local addresses. `SoulRegionStorage` owns immutable checksummed archives and one native compare-and-swap directory head. Both cameras contribute to demanded residency. Each renderer keeps its own local origin and prefixes scenery identities, so distant presentation never rewrites active actor, object, task or receipt coordinates. Remote scenery picks and gizmos cannot execute camp actions.

The current catalog admits 4,096 descriptors and at most 512 closed primitive parts per region. Resident scenery admits 32 regions, with the active simulation included in the 32,768-part/node and 64 MiB estimated working-data budgets. Retained rollback geometry counts toward peak staging. The decoded cache is separately bounded to 8 MiB/32 entries; the app catalog and portable archives have a 128 MiB archive-transfer cap. Camera requests are bounded to 200 m. Camera capacity failures preserve the complete prior preview and report the failure instead of clipping the requested union. Active growth fences obsolete loads and can withdraw scenery before publishing the larger active camp. Active-only overflow reports an explicit presentation failure; canonical collision and simulation state remain resident. These estimates do not measure total VRAM, browser heap or frame rate.

The real GPU renderer passes two scenes at opposite `10^40` sector addresses with preserved centimetre offsets, independent camera movement, addressed restore, rebasing, eviction/reload, publication recovery and complete allocation cleanup. Twelve native storage checks pass checksums, actual OPFS persistence, competing writers, lost write receipts, bounded reads and portable restore. Thirteen residency-owner groups pass identity/schema checks, explicit capacity rejection, rollback staging, supersession, scheduler draining, active growth and disposal. Eleven native app groups pass catalog growth beyond live region capacity, independent `10^60`-sector cameras, unchanged personal knowledge/colliders, corruption rejection, exact portable restore, recovery, active-growth admission and failed writes. Directory-import failure leaves loaded GPU model state and the active world unchanged. This native app fixture uses actual GPU owners and OPFS bytes with a strict CAS test host; the separate storage suite verifies the actual OS storage manager. The existing founder app regression and saved-model compatibility checks pass. Earlier failed receipts stay separate from the corrected reruns; no additional model training or autonomous cross-sector travel was evaluated. The [workflow guide](soul.md#addressed-scenery-regions-29-september-2026) records the controls, literal JSON example and current verification scope.

The active SOUL simulation now uses bounded local coordinates within an immutable exact `soul.simulation-frame.v1`, saved in `soul.world.v2`. Legacy flat projects migrate to a zero frame with their IDs, local positions, pending tasks and sealed personal history preserved. New captured observations, episode/outbox receipts, resource knowledge and group spatial snapshots retain their world frame. Neural arrays and action signatures remain unchanged. Whole-state transaction cloning and full metadata recompilation on source changes remain. Static geometry templates are cached, but sparse uploads do not eliminate compile, validation, clone, persistence or draw costs. Viewport far clipping remains 500 m. Canonical collision/interaction owner records and measured collision envelopes stay resident independently of camera residency; the derived-release workflow can discard unused compiled groups. Imported scenery is a visual preview and is not available to residents as physical terrain or resources.

The address foundation and navigation allocation guard are implemented. New camps can be anchored at enormous exact sectors while rendering and collision use bounded local coordinates. Ordinary transactions and same-identity imports cannot relocate that frame. Native app tests retain pending physical travel through export/import and recovery, and reject rebound histories before storage writes. Navigation admits at most 1,000,000 cells/2,048 per axis before allocation, clips ground to active bounds with body clearance, bounds cached walkable bytes to 8 MiB/100 grids and refuses routes longer than 4,096 points. These are admission limits, not total heap/VRAM or regional routing. See the [physical camp workflow](soul.md#addressed-physical-camp-and-bounded-navigation-29-september-2026).

Current continuation evidence passes 11 frame-owner groups, nine navigation-budget groups, seven native app groups and seven actual GPU renderer groups. Home/stair, group-world/protocol and grounding regressions pass separately. The saved grounded model retains its original checkpoint and held-out result; no new neural training or long-duration civilization acceptance ran. Reports and exact finalization source hashes are indexed separately from the interrupted independent-behavior study.

The next full simulation-streaming slice requires the following dependency order:

1. Design physical region ownership and persistent identities above the fixed frame. Existing local owner positions derive exact addresses without duplicate authoritative position fields. Define verified boundary mapping before allowing a person, compound object, active task or reservation to transfer between owners. A frame re-anchor alone cannot perform that transfer.
2. Partition the canonical owners while pinning active Souls, observation/occlusion regions, carried compounds, work targets, support structures, reservations, route/stair dependencies and unresolved effects. Camera eviction must never turn an obstacle into absent collision geometry.
3. Replace distant rectangular navigation grids with bounded regional routing and verified boundary handoff. Gate movement on loaded physical terrain and required dependencies; an unavailable cell is not empty ground.
4. Persist dirty simulation regions before eviction. Restore owner state and pending receipts before admitting effects. Rebase physical and rendering coordinates consistently without leaking operator knowledge into personal observations.
5. Test crossings, separated cameras, interrupted loads/writes, GPU loss, save/restore and exactly-once resource effects. Measure peak residency, native load latency, frame time, compile/commit cost and neural queues during prolonged travel. Add detail levels and hierarchical visibility against demonstrated bottlenecks. Keep local admission guards while replacing the planner; raising limits alone does not establish resident physical terrain.

The design follows persistent grid cells and independent streaming sources in [Epic's World Partition documentation](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/unreal-engine/world-partition-in-unreal-engine). [Godot's large-world coordinate documentation](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/stable/tutorials/physics/large_world_coordinates.html) explains precision and origin-shifting tradeoffs. [Babylon's large-world documentation](https://github.com/BabylonJS/Documentation/blob/master/content/features/featuresDeepDive/scene/large_world.md) also separates rendering precision from local physics management. Applying those ideas to SOUL is an engineering inference: extend persistent extent while keeping live work bounded. SOUL uses its own Engine/RealmForge implementations. Static distant views are now measured; an infinite civilization simulation and autonomous cross-sector NPC travel remain unimplemented.

#### Reusing WebGPU OS infinite fractals in RealmForge

The local fractal audit finds reusable rendering and precision components. Their current responsibilities remain distinct from physical region ownership.

| Existing implementation | Useful application to SOUL / RealmForge | Required boundary |
|---|---|---|
| `engine/core/gpu/ProgressiveTilePlanner.js`, reused by Fractal `planFractalTiles` | Focus-first deterministic pixel tiles for texture, SDF or other optional view refinement | Plan only a bounded local viewport. Caller retains generation, cancellation and completed publication ownership. |
| Fractal `DeepZoomMath.js` | Arbitrary-decimal complex centers, local mantissa/exponent deltas, precision tiers and cancellable reference generation | Keep physical metre addresses in `BigHierarchicalPosition` and simulation frames. Deep-zoom orbits do not provide terrain, objects or navigation portals. |
| `ProgressiveWorkBudget.js` and canonical `AdaptiveQualityGovernor.js` | Admit optional preparation from measured headroom and queue state; apply hysteresis to a real rendering actuator | Keep resident collision/task dependencies and admission caps independent. CPU samples and queue wall time are not isolated GPU timestamp measurements. |
| Fractal progressive preview/refinement publication | Keep a completed preview while a newer generation prepares; prevent obsolete work from replacing it | CPU scene preparation now cooperates inside regions. GPU refinement publication and resource retirement still require their own measured owner contract. |
| `MathBits.js` Morton ordering | Order nearby bounded cells or work tiles coherently | 2D encoding uses 16 bits per axis; 3D uses 10. Keys wrap outside these ranges and cannot identify global regions. |

RealmForge's `ModelerViewport.diagnosticSnapshot()` currently reports CPU frame encode and real upload counts/bytes. It does not supply a GPU timestamp measurement or a render-scale actuator. Fractal's `onSubmittedWorkDone()` pressure sample includes queue-completion wall time and shared-device contention. The next rendering slice should measure CPU compile/upload, GPU work and queue latency separately, then use the canonical budget planner for optional scenery preparation. Quality must alter actual image/geometry work through one owner, preserve pick identities and permit cancellation; copying a governor alone does not implement that actuator.

The completed first cooperative CPU milestone paced whole region jobs. `SoulPresentationRegions` retained four Engine-scheduled storage reads and one preparation gate across generations, adapting Fractal's cancellable reference-generation pattern. The previous complete preview stayed published until the entire demanded union was ready. Its 21-group protocol and nine-group native receipts remain frozen under `tests/soul/preparation-verification-20260929/`. In that recorded visible-browser fixture, seven new 256-part regions crossed seven completed checkpoints and admitted twelve requested renderer callbacks/submissions. Cumulative preparation including the baseline used 152.4 ms CPU, the longest indivisible job was 28.8 ms and complete publication took 424.7 ms elapsed. These historical observations describe pacing between jobs, not the current incremental implementation.

The existing OS-owned `GpuFrameBudgetBroker.checkpoint({waitForQueue:false,byteLength:0,signal})` provides the native paint opportunity through guarded `gpu.preparationCheckpoint`, retaining GPU permission, mount, generation and device-lease checks. SOUL injects this capability instead of creating a second broker. Yielding stays outside finite synchronous RealmForge transfer scopes because `RealmForgeGpuTransfer` rejects asynchronous callbacks. Engine `TaskScheduler` currently marks a callback's returned Promise complete synchronously, so it cannot own asynchronous region preparation without a separate completion/cancellation contract.

Several grid helpers need adapters or corrections before global reuse. The shader `quadtreeWGSL` computes a recursive UV mask, with no cell identities or neighbors. `SpatialCode` Morton IDs and `ChunkJobCoordinator` encodings have finite wrapping ranges. `getChunkKeyHierarchical()` does not include cell size/LOD in the key and does not validate size. Numeric `RegionManager.chunkToRegion()` uses floor division and positive local modulo; future BigInt parent/neighbor math must retain that negative-coordinate behavior because BigInt division truncates toward zero. SOUL's 100 m cells divide a 10,000 m sector evenly; 32 m cells require explicit partial-boundary handling. `SpatialCode.neighbors2D()` excludes negative cells by contract.

The voxel `AdaptiveChunkBudget` is not the SOUL admission owner: its defaults include thousands of chunks and minimum generation batches far above this app's 32-region profile. Reuse the existing canonical work-budget policy while retaining SOUL's actual part, byte, archive and region limits. Local octree compression and mesh BVHs can accelerate local data; they do not establish physical regional ownership or safe eviction.

All used the same frozen source, five-second decision cadence and default books. The first seed broke an axe at 30 seconds; the second depleted a food site. No neural serving model participated. Every world retained its final checkpoint, with no page, console or source-integrity errors.

| Seed | Controller | Food gathered | Water gathered (L) | Food consumed | Water consumed (L) | Useful prerequisite chains |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 300005 | Random | 0 | 9 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 300005 | Exact context | 2 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| 300005 | Semantic | 2 | 0 | 1 | 2 | 2 |
| 300006 | Random | 2 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 300006 | Exact context | 2 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 300006 | Semantic | 2 | 27 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

All six ended with zero completed shelter stages, deliveries, repairs, chopping, mining, readings, taught practice and learned sequence executions. Shelter proposals were plans only. Health stayed at one with no recorded deprivation during this short horizon. In the second semantic camp, one person held all 27 gathered litres; seven carried no water even though the settlement retained 43 litres including its depot. Carried stock is distinct from access to a reachable shared store. Aggregate resources therefore do not establish successful distribution or cooperation.

The retained episodes also contain seven to thirteen completed group-founding actions per camp. Creating organizations does not establish a durable division of labor. The next behavior investigation should measure offered versus selected productive actions, repeated collecting after personal needs are supplied, reading opportunities, and whether accepted plans reach physical completion. Residents should continue to choose their own work.

The study's competence gate remains false: two seeds and one minute per world do not meet its required evidence. Useful prerequisite chains are controller-neutral observed outcomes, not learned replay. These trials use isolated original world owners with lightweight commit callbacks and no OS viewports; their wall times cannot measure native app throughput. The frozen source predates the presentation optimization while retaining the same v3 decision policy. Sources: `tests/soul/founder-live-bounded-20261001.json`, its manifest and `founder-live-bounded-20261001-worlds/`; source archive `tests/soul/founder-live-v3-source-20261001.zip`.

Delivered teaching supplies zero borrowed personal successes. The bounded practice mechanism now lets a recipient try an applicable taught chain, recording personal results separately from demonstrated learned execution. The saved two-start budget and eight-decision cooldown prevent endless imposed rehearsal. Test voluntary teaching, actual practice and later independent reuse over longer unforced runs before claiming effective teaching of complete skills.

After grounded skill transfer passes, add renewable water/food production, measured regrowth, storage/spoilage and balanced rates. Then test voluntary specialization, exchanged commitments, teaching and family care over longer horizons. Connect live camera/OCR observations and paired-view identity/occlusion tasks before claiming visual grounding. Speech, wider architecture and more varied buildings keep separate acceptance gates. The existing renderer, dictionary and storylets remain shared foundations throughout.
