## Understand node and runtime support

Ambient Studio separates authoring vocabulary from installed runtime capability. The node library labels that difference instead of showing a successful compile badge for content the runtime cannot draw.

| Composite V2 support | Nodes | Current behavior |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Executable | `source.shader`, `source.showcase`, `effect.color-grade`, `effect.blur`, `effect.bloom`, `layer.compose`, `output.wallpaper` | Compiles into ordered procedural layers. Effects run only on one procedural source at a time and remain inside a bounded shader sample budget. |
| Executable shader contributions | `code.wgsl.*` connected to a composed `source.shader` | Compiles persisted source contributions into that shader's saved template. |
| Implicit signals | `input.time`, `input.pointer` | Records the bounded runtime dependency. The procedural runtime owns the corresponding live signal contract. |
| Executable media | `source.image`, `source.video` | Verified project assets render through native texture layers with fit, placement, opacity, and muted video playback. Old descriptors without complete asset records require reopening and saving. |
| Runtime pending | `input.audio`, `effect.parallax`, all `particle.*`, `voxel.*`, and `scene.*` nodes | The required composite runtime ABI or compiler is not installed. A required unsupported node fails compilation before preview or desktop activation. |

The node library displays **RUNTIME PENDING** on unsupported authoring nodes. Classic Living Matter and Voxel Shrine retain their dedicated particle and scene implementations. Spatial Gaussian projects use their own geometry, source, processing and output graph with a shared preview/desktop driver. Native V3 component graphs execute through their corresponding program, simulation or particle-field driver. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientCompositeCompiler.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/WebGPUCompositeAmbientDriver.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialProject.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientWallpaperV2Catalog.js`.)

## Project and runtime contracts

Ambient Studio separates editable projects, executable plans, and portable packages:

| Contract | Purpose | Important limits |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `particle-realms.ambient-project.v2` | Editable metadata, assets, layers, graph, timeline, published controls, quality, accessibility, audit fields, revision, and content hash | 8 MiB canonical JSON; 510 assets; 4,096 layers and nodes; 16,384 connections; 4,096 tracks; 65,536 keyframes |
| `particle-realms.ambient-composite-plan.v2` | Canonical kernel-owned plan emitted by the layered graph compiler | 512 KiB; 1â€“32 ordered procedural, solid, image, or video layers; content-derived hash |
| `particle-realms.ambient-runtime-plan.v3` | Native program, simulation or particle-field execution plan | Validated recipe settings and bounded authored program or appearance functions; content-derived hash |
| `particle-realms.ambient-spatial-plan.v1` | Native spatial Gaussian renderer plan | Validated settings, immutable asset descriptors, geometry budget, and content-derived hash |
| `particle-realms.ambient-package.v1` | Portable `.ambient` ZIP containing one canonical V2 project and its declared project-owned assets | 512 entries; 512 MiB uncompressed total; 256 MiB per entry |
| `particle-realms.ambient-project.v1` and `particle-realms.ambient-plan.v1` | Compatibility project and executable plan for restricted shader examples | 256 KiB V1 project; pure Paint shader function and the existing 64-byte uniform ABI |

`compileAmbientCompositeProject()` validates the complete V2 project and typed graph, resolves only nodes reachable from `output.wallpaper`, compiles supported procedural effects, and emits `particle-realms.ambient-composite-plan.v2`. It fails closed on cycles, invalid ports, missing required inputs, missing assets, unsupported output-path nodes, ambiguous layer bindings, and budget violations. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientProjectV2.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientCompositeCompiler.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/schema/CompositeAmbientContract.js`.)

## Save projects and revisions safely

Layered V2 projects use this operator-scoped layout:

```text
/user/Ambient Studio/projects/<project-id>/
â”œâ”€â”€ project.ambient.json
â”œâ”€â”€ draft.ambient.json
â”œâ”€â”€ revisions/
â”‚   â””â”€â”€ 00000001.ambient.json
â”œâ”€â”€ assets/
â”‚   â””â”€â”€ <64-hex-sha256>.<extension>
â””â”€â”€ legacy-migration-receipt.json
```

`project.ambient.json` is the project head. `draft.ambient.json` is the current saved draft. Numbered revision files are immutable restore points. Imported assets use their complete SHA-256 digest in both the generated `asset-<64-hex-sha256>` record ID and content-addressed path. The repository verifies every asset again after writing and when reading it for export. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioProjectRepository.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientAssetImporter.js`.)

Saving an existing V2 draft or revision requires both the expected project revision and expected project content hash. The repository compares that logical base with the stored head, then uses `storage.writeAtomic` with the observed storage hash. A concurrent change produces a conflict instead of overwriting newer work. Every successful write receives an exact readback check. (Source: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioProjectRepository.js`.)

**Use as Wallpaper** saves the current editable source as an immutable revision, then compiles and activates that same source. You do not need to save separately first. Editing controls temporarily lock during the operation; preview-only updates do not cancel it. An authored change that reaches the session aborts activation and preserves the newer edit. If the source commit already completed, its verified revision remains the base for a retry. An older pending compile cannot restore the pre-save revision after adoption. (Source: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`.)

The project library asks before leaving unsaved changes. It blocks deletion when the project owns the active desktop wallpaper. Restoring an old revision creates a new revision instead of overwriting history. Legacy drafts and revisions remain discoverable for explicit migration; the migration receipt records the source hash and leaves the legacy source undeleted. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioProjectRepository.js`.)

## Import assets and portable packages

Layered V2 projects accept these local, self-contained assets:

- PNG, JPEG, WebP, and GIF images.
- MP4 and WebM video.
- Ogg, MP3, and WAV audio.
- Binary GLB models with no external texture or buffer references.

Layered import checks the declared type, file extension, magic bytes, decode metadata, size, dimensions, duration, and SHA-256 digest. It rejects active document and script formats. Image and video layers now execute in the composite renderer. Spatial source imports accept PNG, JPEG, WebP, MP4, and WebM through that same validator, up to 256 MiB. A missing browser MIME type can use the extension, but the bytes must still match. Decoding has a bounded timeout and cancellation; a newer import or project change retires the earlier operation. Original bytes, dimensions, video duration and full content identity remain stored. Gaussian PLY and SPLAT files become canonical geometry. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientAssetImporter.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialTools.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientCompositeMedia.js`.)

A V2 export uses the `.ambient` extension and `application/vnd.particle-realms.ambient+zip` media type. The package contains `ambient-package.json`, `project.ambient.json`, and only declared content-addressed assets. Import verifies canonical JSON, project identity and content hash, asset hashes and sizes, entry counts, byte totals, archive paths, duplicate paths, undeclared entries, and external references before installation. A package must pass the real parser to receive the in-memory verification marker accepted by the repository. A user-authored `verified: true` field is not sufficient. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientPackage.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioProjectRepository.js`.)

Legacy V1 particle, scene, and shader projects continue to import and export `.ambient.json`. The supplied standalone experiments can also import through the legacy scene converter. Its conversion report identifies the native preset or selected spatial/media layer and any unsupported custom layer stacks, GLSL, or broadcast settings. The original JSON and embedded assets remain archived in the project. Arbitrary legacy shader stacks do not execute as native WGSL. Package installation requires the complete operator project-storage capability surface and an unused destination project ID. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/LegacySceneConversion.js`.)

### Frame imported images and choose video clips

Image and video source nodes in layered projects expose **Artwork fit** and **Artwork position**. Use cover to fill the output, contain to show the full source, or fill for deliberate stretching. Choose a fixed edge or custom focal X/Y in the range 0â€“1. Source bytes stay unchanged; the saved node controls the framing in Studio, wallpaper playback and export. Spatial sources use their existing camera fit and composition controls. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientCompositeCompiler.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/schema/CompositeAmbientContract.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientCompositeMedia.js`.)

A video source can save `sourceClip: {"startSeconds": 0.5, "endSeconds": 2.5}`. End can be `null` to use the source end; clearing the clip restores the full video. Spatial **Source media** controls expose the range in seconds. Scrub spans the selected range, and loop or back-and-forth playback stays within it. A range that becomes empty against the decoded duration reports an error. Local recorder WebM files with omitted duration receive a bounded decoder probe. First-frame preparation and later uploads wait for completed decoding rather than treating a requested seek time as a ready frame. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioWorkspace.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCore.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialVideoPlayback.js`.)

**Use current video frame** selects the decoded preview frame in the saved source node. Depth painting, reconstruction and background preparation display their reference time. Applying preparation pins source playback to that frame and records the original video asset identity and timestamp in the prepared asset. The original video remains stored; source controls can resume it. A static depth map does not track moving objects after playback resumes. (Source: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialTools.js`.)

## Preview and apply safely

Each project family uses the same corresponding driver for preview and desktop execution. Layered projects use the ordered composite driver; native and spatial projects use their dedicated drivers. Ambient Studio acquires an app-scoped surface and the active GPU-device generation through guarded GPU services. The kernel owns the device, canvas configuration, frame admission, and surface release. The preview reports success only after the driver publishes a running state for the expected plan hash and submits at least one frame. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientCompositePreviewRenderer.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientRuntimeV3PreviewRenderer.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/WebGPUCompositeAmbientDriver.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/SurfaceManager.js`.)

**Test on Desktop** previews the compiled plan without making it the saved wallpaper selection. Spatial project assets and their draft are persisted first so the desktop can resolve the same verified media. **Stop test**, closing Studio and failed activation restore the preceding wallpaper only while that operation still owns the desktop publication. A newer selection is retained, including a static wallpaper or another publication of the same source. The kernel rechecks publication ownership after asynchronous hooks before rollback. Desktop actions require the full OS shell; the standalone app host provides authoring and preview. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/AmbientEngine.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/AmbientActivation.js`, `webgpu-os/shell/Desktop.js`.)

An explicit wallpaper choice in Theme Manager replaces the authored wallpaper and persists that choice. Accent, contrast, motion, or transparency changes preserve the authored wallpaper when the wallpaper selection itself did not change. (Source: `webgpu-os/kernel/ThemeEngine.js`.)

## Ocean views

### Procedural water version 2

New **Ocean daylight**, **Ocean moonlight**, **Ocean swell**, **Moonlit water**, **Sea of Memory** and **Ripple horizon · studio** graphs save a versioned wind-field recipe and pure spectral-density functions. The engine derives displacement, velocity, tangents, horizontal compression and directional slope statistics from that saved source. Three complementary frequency bands use 256, 32 and 4 metre domains. Each starts at 128 by 128 samples. The runtime can prepare 256 by 256 samples only after the existing quality governor admits measured GPU headroom. The same saved seed and physical frequencies preserve wave phase. (Sources: `engine/render/water/WaterFieldRecipe.js`, `engine/render/water/WaterFieldService.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanWaterField.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientRuntimeV3Performance.js`.)

Seven indexed clipmap levels generate 64 cells per side, weld adjacent boundaries and blend their resolved wavelengths. Linear mipmaps store slope means and directional second moments. Anisotropic filtering uses four to eight taps for elongated footprints; unresolved slope energy broadens the normalized Beckmann reflection distribution. The material uses the engine's exact dielectric Fresnel, finite sun or moon discs and the saved sky. It retains HDR grading. The former independent twelve-wave ripple layer is absent from these factory graphs. (Sources: `engine/render/water/WaterClipmap.js`, `engine/render/water/WaterFieldShaders.js`, `engine/render/water/WaterOptics.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanComposition.js`.)

New ocean graphs also save visible-normal Beckmann sampling in **Water optics and pigment** (`ocean-water`). This owner combines `WATER_OPTICS_WGSL` with the separate `WATER_VISIBLE_OPTICS_WGSL` helpers. **Sky and clouds** (`ocean-sky`) filters cloud noise using the reflected angular cone before reflection integration, replacing unresolved cloud octaves with their mean. The cone uses camera-ray derivatives and slope covariance, without counting derivatives of the already filtered water normal twice. Quiet aliases forward the filtered atmosphere hook to their own saved sky. Existing custom sky source remains unchanged during a selected water upgrade; its saved atmosphere supplies incident light directly. Earlier and finite water helper libraries retain their existing source. (Sources: `engine/render/water/WaterOptics.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanWaterField.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanAliasComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientWaterUpgrade.js`.)

Retained foam starts empty. Saved compression thresholds qualify crest birth, recorded droplet impacts deposit over a finite area, and foam density and age travel in surface coordinates before decaying. The bounded 256-particle solver queries the same field. Automatic emission searches eligible crests instead of choosing a hashed foreground location. Spectrum, fine detail, mesh, light, optics, foam, spray and pointer response remain separate editable source owners. Runtime textures are derived data. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanState.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanMeshLane.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanComposition.js`.)

New canal, puddle, wet-road, terrain and Sky garden coatings, and **Rain garden** graphs save `ambientFiniteWaterStateVersion()` returning `1u`. Their field owner uses the shared seeded directional spectrum and complementary 256, 32 and 4 metre bands at 128 by 128 samples. Geometry saves the bounded physical domain, wet mask and coordinate transform. Separate source owners control spectrum, optics, foam and contact response. Two linear mipmapped textures retain foam density and age; eligible compression and recorded finite-area impacts supply birth, while saved current, decay and production functions govern transport. Contact and rendering use the same saved camera and intersections, with canonical DOM coordinates converted by the contact source. Rain garden's two visible ring cycles share saved centres and phases with recorded impact deposition; their source filters sub-cell impacts over a finite footprint. Deleting a contribution selects its saved neutral fallback. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientFiniteWaterAuthoring.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientShowcaseShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/FiniteAmbientWaterLane.js`, `engine/render/water/WaterFoamKernels.js`.)

New Midnight Downpour puddles save **Perceptual water roughness** at 0.24 in the separate optics owner. This broadens reflected lamp highlights while retaining the saved lights and scene grading. Canal optics retain their 0.08 default. Both controls remain editable; existing saved source keeps its authored value. (Source: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOriginalComposition.js`.)

These finite adapters preserve the existing implicit scene geometry and pigment presentation. They do not generate a clipmap or a separate airborne particle pool, and their field and foam grids remain at 128 by 128 samples. The host supplies the device, frame buffer, shader time, encoder and submission. The complete spectrum and history allocation is 5,822,920 bytes; deleting the field uses the 184-byte neutral binding, with 349,800 bytes including retained histories and owner buffers. Spatial water version 2 caches its saved finite source through the same field service. Its bounded lakes follow opaque bed triangles, rivers follow their saved channel, and waterfalls use falling sheets with owned impact spray. Reliable opaque bed geometry enables scene capture before water and transparent splats; absent bed geometry retains depth pigment. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/FiniteAmbientWaterLane.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientFiniteWaterHost.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialWaterOperations.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`, `engine/render/water/WaterFieldNeutral.js`.)

New spatial factories save `waterStateVersion: 1` and a separate foam owner with saved production, transport, decay and finite-area impact functions. Two linear mipmapped array textures retain density and age in each interface's source coordinates. Masks come from the actual saved water triangles, so dry ridges and channel banks receive no foam. Histories start at 128 by 128 samples per owner; construction can select 64 by 64 before allocation when replacement residency requires it. All levels, masks and owner buffers count toward the shared water budget. A falling sheet records flow at its valid receiver independently of its visible spray count; deleting the receiver or disconnecting its link removes that deposition. The contact owner saves independent click and optional hover gains and code. Contact rays intersect saved base triangles with opaque occlusion; the hit point approximates the small displaced surface. Successful host submission commits a history swap. Abort, Still and capture resizing retain committed density and age, and a click arriving during the first admitted frame or Still is processed once. (Sources: `engine/render/water/WaterFoamKernels.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialWaterFoam.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialWaterShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialWaterSurface.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialWaterFoamSource.js`.)

Spatial refraction captures opaque color after scene and shadow rendering. A second pass draws only those opaque triangles into an `r32float` color texture, using equal depth testing against the original read-only `depth32float` attachment. Water samples the captured depth at texel centres through a nearest sampler. This preserves the actual visible bed depth without reading or sampling a depth texture, which compatibility adapters restrict. Water renders before transparent splats. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialWaterShaders.js`.)

The default diorama's falling sheet ends on a dry bank above the saved lake bed, outside its wet triangles. Its receiver therefore rejects deposition and impact spray. Moving the saved endpoint or editing the bed can establish an eligible receiver; the runtime does not invent water beneath that geometry. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialDiorama.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialWaterSurface.js`, `tests/run_ambient_water_observation_camera_cpu.py`.)

Opening a saved project keeps its existing implementation. **Preview water upgrade** lists the dependent source owners and requires an explicit selection. Preview is one undoable session edit. **Keep upgrade** requires a submitted GPU frame for the current candidate hash; **Undo preview** remains available on failure. Unselected props, cameras, terrain, palettes and source stay intact. Upgrading an older finite ocean source retains its existing renderer; newly created ocean factories use the shared indexed mesh lane. Offline players collect the actual renderer's local module dependencies. Imported media, captured clouds, window rain, coffee, ink, liquid metal and volumetric fluid demos keep their existing paths. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientWaterUpgrade.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientNativePlayerExport.js`.)

Older spatial V2 graphs without the retained-state marker also receive an explicit preview offer. With existing operation owners, it changes the selected geometry marker and connected old foam source, adds a missing contact owner, and preserves saved field, optics and spray source. It retains deleted or disconnected foam owners. Reopening or compiling these older graphs does not perform that upgrade. (Source: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientWaterUpgrade.js`.)

Older finite V2 graphs and raw Rain garden source also receive a selected retained-state preview. It preserves their actual saved field body and coefficients in an `analytic-cache-v2` field, discloses the query rename and added foam/contact owners, and reuses the saved camera prefix. Unselected source and optics remain unchanged. Historical non-affine coordinate mappings retain their original behaviour, so cached derivatives approximate those mappings; new factory mappings use affine physical coordinates. Unknown source boundaries block the preview instead of substituting factory source. Opening an older document performs no migration. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientFiniteWaterUpgrade.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientFiniteWaterAuthoring.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientWaterUpgrade.js`.)

For pre-V2 canal, puddle and wet-road graphs, the same selected preview replaces the disclosed water functions and adds field, foam and contact infrastructure in one undoable edit. The camera bridge moves actual saved camera text rather than regenerating it. Earlier Atmospheric depth and Sky garden graphs that contain only dry terrain receive a blocked offer: a separate water geometry, mask and bed must first be authored. Their original source remains unchanged. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientWaterUpgrade.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientFiniteWaterUpgrade.js`, `tests/ambient-finite-water-upgrade.test.js`.)

The runtime uses the host device, frame clock, command encoder and submission lifecycle. One ledger per physical device caps water residency at 64 MiB. It reserves construction before the first allocation and counts active owners, pending fields, replacement targets, refraction captures and separate mip-generation scratch textures. Cancellation keeps the reservation until construction cleanup and its queue fence settle. A failed retirement fence retains its bytes until device loss. Quality changes reduce capture resolution before removing filtering or clearing foam. Diagnostics expose residency, selected detail and compile failures. Native Runtime V3 also reports queue pressure and measured timestamp availability through the canonical profiler. A configured 60 FPS target is not a performance guarantee. Full shoreline simulation, volumetric pressure solves and screen-space reflections remain separate work. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientRuntimeV3Residency.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/WebGPUAmbientRuntimeV3Driver.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanMeshLane.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientRuntimeV3Performance.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`.)

Program water opts into retained phase through the saved pure `ambientWaterSurfaceVersion()` function returning `2u`. The shared water clock prepares a frame without changing committed phase and advances only after successful submission. Abort, Still mode and suspension preserve phase; speed changes affect subsequent increments. Recompiling identical water source for grading retains its phase, field and histories. Candidate construction captures the canonical click serial so a new owner cannot replay an earlier click; a new event arriving on its first admitted frame is eligible, including serial rollover. Older unmarked programs retain their existing clock behavior. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientProgramWaterClock.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/WebGPUAmbientRuntimeV3Driver.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientPreviewRenderer.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/WebGPUAmbientProgramDriver.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/FiniteAmbientWaterLane.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialWaterFoam.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanState.js`.)

Versioned water producers use the existing frame coordinator's `cadenceMode: 'phase'` policy at the saved target rate. It carries the remainder between display frames instead of rounding each interval upward. At 144 Hz, a 60 FPS target can alternate two and three display frames, giving 13.89 and 20.83 ms intervals while averaging 60 FPS. Consequently, delivered-frame p95 can exceed 16.7 ms even when measured GPU and CPU work fit that budget. Missed deadlines, unsuccessful submissions and long encoding stalls discard accumulated credits; visibility, pause and target changes reset the deadline. Other consumers retain the default minimum-interval policy. The guarded registration and update paths accept only these bounded cadence modes and retain their existing owner and lifecycle checks. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/GpuFrameCoordinator.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/Syscalls.js`, `tests/kernel/gpu-frame-coordinator.test.js`, `tests/virtual-realm/m2-guarded-frame-telemetry-source.test.js`.)

The original implementation follows the filtered geometric, normal and reflectance hierarchy in [Bruneton's ocean research](https://evasion.inrialpes.fr/~Eric.Bruneton/) and directional moment filtering in [LEAN mapping](https://userpages.cs.umbc.edu/olano/papers/lean/). These are research references, without imported water code or texture assets.

### Earlier water documents

The following describes saved graphs without the version 2 field marker. They retain their saved source when opened; starting a fresh factory or choosing the explicit upgrade selects the new implementation.

**Ocean daylight**, **Ocean moonlight** and **Ocean swell** use an actual displaced triangle mesh. Its radial spacing concentrates geometry near the camera and increases spacing toward the horizon. The backing resolution and saved mesh-detail control bound the grid to 128 radial cells by 192 angular cells. A depth attachment resolves wave occlusion and local droplets. These entries appear in the Atmospheres collection; Ocean daylight also appears in Featured. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanMeshLane.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanMeshShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientCollectionNativePresets.js`.)

The new mesh presets save 48 explicit, seeded wind-spectrum modes in their wave node. Wavelength bands distribute their integrated energy among several directions so one random coefficient cannot dominate the surface. One finite spectral model supplies horizontal and vertical displacement, tangent normals, material velocity, unresolved slope variance, and the horizontal deformation Jacobian. World-position queries invert that same displaced surface. Pixel filtering uses each wave's projected phase derivatives, preserving detail along the narrow axis of a grazing pixel. Wave height, wind speed, direction, water depth and choppiness are source-bound controls; editing saved mode code does not regenerate it from a preset name or seed. The model is directly evaluated, not an FFT. (Source: `engine/render/water/OceanSpectrum.js`.)

Retained foam uses two 128 × 128 textures in the wave surface's rest coordinates. Compression generates foam; authored drift transports it, decay removes it, and local droplets can deposit foam when they rejoin the prescribed surface. The foam node owns production, threshold, onset width, lifetime, region, drift, patch detail, breakup and material code. Near detail resolves into rounded pores and broken clusters; unresolved detail uses filtered population coverage. Foam receives environment and direct lighting. It starts empty and develops during playback. A separate bounded pool of 256 particles uses the engine's shared PBF kernels, three density-projection iterations per step, a 1/120-second timestep, and at most four steps per frame. The complete local neighbor set is evaluated without a truncated neighbor list. Click, hover and drag forces are saved source functions. This exchanges material with a prescribed wave surface; it does not conserve the mass of an entire simulated ocean or solve shoreline breaking. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanState.js`, `engine/sim/fluids/PbfKernels.js`.)

Thirteen connected node groups own the spectrum, independent wind ripples, mesh, camera, sun or moon, shared noise, clouds, water optics, foam, splashes, pointer response, distance haze and display color transfer. Cloud and foam nodes share the explicit noise component; deleting clouds does not remove foam detail. Clouds use a bounded three-dimensional density slab with light extinction. Unresolved horizon detail converges to mean cloud extinction, with a continuous transition into the reflected lower hemisphere. Each look saves its own cloud coverage, formation scale and seed. Fine ripples have their own direction, strength and filtered slope variance. The output node converts tone-mapped linear light to sRGB for the unorm canvas. Their complete function source and neutral deletion fallbacks travel with the project and offline player. Earlier saved function libraries retain their original entrypoint behavior when newer hooks are absent. Mesh and retained simulation state share one clock. Still and suspension freeze it; changing only global playback or grading settings can reuse the lane, and resizing preserves the foam and particles. Editing shader source recompiles its lane. Water optics use sky reflection and the engine's Fresnel/GGX functions; scene-object reflection, refraction, underwater rendering and bathymetry-driven surf are not implemented in these open-ocean presets. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientOceanComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanMeshShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/WebGPUAmbientRuntimeV3Driver.js`.)

New **Moonlit water**, **Sea of Memory** and **Ripple horizon · studio** projects share a directional ocean model. Larger swells and shorter wind waves travel independently, with wavelength-dependent speed. The same filtered height function supplies the displaced surface and its shading derivatives. Wave detail too small for a pixel contributes to reflection roughness. The factory saves the complete shader contributions into the project; reopening a saved source graph keeps that graph's authored implementation. Choose the preset again to start with its updated factory version. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanSurface.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientMaterialShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientNativeSurfaceShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientCollectionCatalog.js`.)

Use the wave component to edit height, wavelength, direction, directional spread, short wind waves and crest sharpness. Camera components set eye height and horizon or pitch; separate components own roughness, moonlight, sky, mist and crest foam. Removing the moon removes its visible and reflected light. Removing the wave component removes its displacement and wind-wave normals. Wave source and its conservative height, slope and curvature bounds are saved together; keep those bounds consistent when writing a custom height function. Pointer and click responses retain their own saved source components. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientMaterialComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientNativeLaneComposition.js`.)

Water lighting reuses the engine's Fresnel, GGX and masking functions. Visible sky and reflected atmosphere use the same authored environment, while the moon's direct reflection is evaluated separately. The surface intersection and environment filtering have bounded work; this is a finite analytic wave approximation. The native distant ridge remains an authored silhouette. Deep-water color remains an artistic surface treatment. These wallpapers do not yet simulate spectral FFT seas, bathymetry-driven breakers, retained foam transport, airborne spray, underwater scattering, or scene-object reflection and refraction. (Sources: `engine/render/shaders/modules/chunks/pbr_materials.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanSurface.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientNativeSurfaceShaders.js`.)

Whitecap components expose coverage strength, breaking threshold, lifetime, patch scale and drift speed. Five recent samples of the authored wave compression signal reconstruct patches with decay; the engine's filtered world-space noise breaks up their coverage. Matte foam replaces the reflective water beneath it. This is a bounded analytic history approximation with no retained foam buffer or SPH coupling. The foam node saves its helper code and material contribution; deleting it removes whitewater, and deleting the wave node or setting wave height to zero removes its source. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/AmbientOceanSurface.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientMaterialComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientNativeLaneComposition.js`, `engine/render/shaders/modules/chunks/noise2d.js`.)

The upgrade follows the separation of geometric swells, surface detail and matching derivatives described in [NVIDIA's water simulation chapter](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems/part-i-natural-effects/chapter-1-effective-water-simulation-physical-models). Further realism needs explicit scene inputs: [Epic's water model](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/single-layer-water-shading-model-in-unreal-engine) uses depth and color for refraction, while [Crest's foam settings](https://docs.crest.waveharmonic.com/Assets/SimulationSettings/FoamSettings.html) distinguish wave production, decay and depth-based shoreline foam. These are research references; their source code and assets are not included.

The [shallow-water and dispersive-wave study](https://research.nvidia.com/labs/prl/shallow-water-simulation/) is a future simulation reference: it separates retained bulk flow from dispersive surface waves and recombines their flux. Implementing it requires conservative depth/momentum state, bathymetry, wet/dry handling and validated transforms. The [box-constrained pressure study](https://cs.uwaterloo.ca/~c2batty/papers/Takahashi2024/Takahashi2024.pdf) and [extended cut-cell study](https://cgl.ethz.ch/publications/papers/paperChen20a.php) address downstream pressure and thin-liquid geometry. None of those solvers is implemented in these wallpapers; the current finite-mode waves and local PBF pool retain their explicit scope.

The engine's existing water paths have different roles. The playground SPH demo runs a local particle fluid with depth/thickness surface reconstruction; its foam tint does not provide a persistent whitewater simulation. Texture Studio generates color, normal, metallic/roughness and AO maps; its **Foam** preset describes a porous solid material. Spatial diorama water already uses actual terrain-clipped triangles, two traveling vertex waves and matching normals. That finite mesh is separate from these ocean wallpapers. (Sources: `tests/playground/src/demos/sphFluid/index.js`, `tests/playground/src/demos/sphFluid/shaders.js`, `tests/playground/src/demos/textureStudio/index.js`, `engine/assets/material/procedural/ProceduralPbrTexture.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialDiorama.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientShaders.js`.)

The new mesh uses radial sampling, a technique discussed in [NVIDIA's vertex displacement chapter](https://developer.nvidia.com/gpugems/gpugems2/part-ii-shading-lighting-and-shadows/chapter-18-using-vertex-texture-displacement). [Epic's water meshing guide](https://dev.epicgames.com/documentation/en-us/unreal-engine/water-meshing-system-and-surface-rendering-in-unreal-engine) describes a different approach using camera-centered tiles and gradual LOD transitions. The current implementation has no tile quadtree or shoreline depth input. Its local PBF kernels are shared with the playground fluid; no external water source code or assets were imported.

## Spatial artwork and depth preparation

Spatial templates provide liquid flow, shatter and reform, temporal ribbons, elastic structure, surface ripples, and orbital gather. Particles retain canonical anchors and source colors. The renderer supports anisotropic covariance, spherical harmonics, calibrated projection, depth sorting, masks, bounded structure deformation, and baked background plates. Camera controls and color, depth, normal, identity, coverage, and confidence views help inspect the result. A single image produces an editable depth lift; it does not recover hidden surfaces or constitute a trained 4D reconstruction. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCore.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`.)

The image-based spatial examples retain the supplied mountain and waterfall artwork with its original authored depth map. That depth is hand-authored, not measured or inferred. The gallery labels these entries **Spatial templates** and **Media templates**: they demonstrate different editable responses using the same sample artwork. The diorama has editable terrain, water, foliage and pavilion geometry. Its new terrain node saves engine heightfield samples and renders an opaque triangle surface through the existing spatial mesh pipeline. Trees and the linked waterfall sample that same field for their attachment heights. Old nodes without the optional heightfield, mesh or grounded-waterfall fields retain their original geometry. Image/video imports start without a physical border; **Artwork frame** in **Camera & inspection** enables it explicitly. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialExample.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialDiorama.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialDioramaSchema.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioWorkspace.js`.)

**Atmospheric depth**, **Sky Garden** and **Gaussian Scene Explorer** use terrain baked by the engine's seeded noise library, coherent tectonic initialization, hydraulic erosion and conservative thermal erosion. Generation controls include the seed, physical extent, grid, plate and rain settings, thermal surface material and transfer rate. Change those saved inputs, then choose **Regenerate terrain** on the terrain node to run the engine through the app's guarded GPU device. Progress and cancellation are visible. Editing source or parameters, changing projects or closing Studio cancels the operation; failed or stale results retain the existing saved samples. Undo restores the previous field. (Sources: `engine/world/generation/TerrainBake.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientTerrainAuthoring.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientStudioApp.js`.)

The node document owns the baked result. The spatial node retains its numeric height and relative drainage arrays; its props attach to the actual rendered triangles at the selected mesh resolution. The two shader scenes save compact, quantized display samples directly in editable WGSL and share an exact bilinear-cell intersection routine. Their editable normal radius smooths shading using neighboring measured heights without changing the terrain intersections. Range dimensions, relief, camera and materials remain editable node parameters. Removing the connected terrain node removes its visible mountains; recreating the saved node and connections restores the same source. Regeneration replaces only the marked generated source block, preserving surrounding artist code. Saved samples recreate exactly; a full hydraulic regeneration can vary because concurrent sediment transfers change ordering. Drainage means cumulative rain-particle cell visitation, normalized logarithmically; it does not measure river volume or water depth. Clouds remain authored visual components. This bake does not run the engine's wind erosion or volumetric cloud simulation. (Sources: `engine/world/generation/TerrainHeightfield.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientTerrainAuthoring.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientMaterialComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientIllustratedComposition.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialDiorama.js`.)

Sediment placement and water highlights are artistic shading, without a simulated water depth, discharge or guaranteed continuous river. ### Choose a source that supports the desired perspective

Ambient Studio distinguishes source coverage from artistic appearance. A single image supplies visible surfaces; depth can separate them, but cannot measure a tree's hidden branches or back. A 360Â° video supplies directions around its capture point, without translation parallax. Registered multi-view depth supplies observed three-dimensional surfaces. Generated trees supply their complete authored structure. **Compare original source** displays the retained photo, video or reference capture independently of the renderer. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientImmersionControls.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCameraRig.js`.)

| Source | Perspective and depth | Remaining limit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Single-image relief | Bounded inspection of lifted source-visible surfaces | Missing surfaces remain unknown; inferred relative depth has no measured metre scale |
| Equirectangular or cubemap media | Rotational viewing from one origin | No fabricated translation or stereoscopic depth |
| Calibrated RGB-D or stereo capture | Saved pinhole camera and registered world-space splats | Supplied calibration controls accuracy; unsupported and unseen surfaces stay absent |
| Forest presence | Eye-level route through generated terrain and separate complete trees | Generated geometry does not reconstruct the tree photographed in an imported image |

Select **Source projection** after importing suitable media. Equirectangular media must contain a full sphere in a 2:1 image. A cubemap uses six horizontal square faces in `+X, -X, +Y, -Y, +Z, -Z` order. Both render camera rays and disable translation. Changing the projection saves the choice in the source and appearance nodes. Media imports start with neutral response and grading and clear the previous generated sky and distance fog. Later projection changes preserve the current artistic response and grading while clearing generated sky and fog. A perspective movie or screenshot is not converted into a measured 360Â° scene by selecting this control. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialTools.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientImmersionControls.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientMipmaps.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/schema/AmbientSpatialContract.js`.)

### Save a world camera and inspect captured appearance

**Saved viewpoint & movement** stores the camera's base position, target, up direction, eye height, movement limits, clipping distances and optional original-pixel lens calibration. Orbit cameras inspect a target; world cameras look from a saved eye. Movement buttons and the saved modified-drag binding edit or inspect this rig. **Save inspected viewpoint** writes the actual rendered pose, including gesture changes, into the camera node. Bounds and source envelopes constrain movement. Their coverage score is authored metadata or the capture's support score, not an independently calibrated probability of correct reconstruction. Older projects without `cameraRig` keep their historical orbit and framing. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientImmersionControls.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCameraRig.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialResponse.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`.)

This complete `cameraRig` value places a generated scene's eye 1.65 scene units above its saved base. `unitScale` states metres per scene unit; use a measured scale for a metric capture. Set this JSON on the camera node in **Code / Plan** or its node inspector. A rig's position and lens do not resize its geometry. (Source: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCameraRig.js`.)

```json
{
  "version": 1,

  "position": [0, 0, -3],

  "up": [0, 1, 0],
  "unitScale": 1,
  "eyeHeight": 1.65,
  "near": 0.05,
  "far": 120,
  "bounds": { "min": [-2, 0, -5], "max": [2, 3, 1] },
  "intrinsics": null,
  "path": null,
  "source": {
    "kind": "procedural", "confidence": 1,

```

**Record path start** and **Record 12 second return path** save positions and targets as ordered keyframes. JSON can author other bounded durations and paths; looped paths must close their pose. New cloud imports retain source coordinates through explicit `cloudFrame` and fit the measured bounds. Calibrated captures open at their first supplied pose with its original lens. **Reconstruct surface splats** retains its source-pixel lens and identifies the result as single-view relief. Metric-frame density selection uses the exact requested bounded count with aligned canonical IDs. Missing optional fields do not migrate older documents. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialTools.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCore.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialReconstruction.js`.)

Studio PLY import subtracts a double-precision world `origin` before storing local Float32 positions. The matching `cloudFrame.origin` keeps the fitted camera and GPU geometry local, preserving small separations at large world coordinates. Canonical PLY export writes double world positions and an origin comment for reopening, with supplied group IDs and confidence. SPLAT files already contain Float32 coordinates; import cannot recover precision absent from those bytes. Both importers retain at most 200,000 records through deterministic stride reduction and record a warning when reducing a larger source. The canonical cloud means the retained import, not discarded input records. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialIO.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCore.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialTools.js`.)

New captures start in **faithful** appearance with neutral saved motion and grading. The faithful renderer preserves imported color, opacity, covariance scale and available spherical harmonics while bypassing artistic relighting, tint and motion blur. Faithful captured sources also suppress generated mesh lighting, surface detail and sun shadows. **Preserve captured appearance** clears inherited generated sky and distance fog for captured, relief and panoramic sources. In generated scenes, **Reset extra appearance grading** preserves the authored sky, mesh materials, lighting and shadows. **Enable artistic grading** changes saved appearance values explicitly. Objects remain editable through supplied Gaussian group IDs: an object selection can hide, translate, uniformly scale or change opacity for its groups. These selections do not infer semantic objects, and their transforms do not retrain directional spherical harmonics. The canonical asset stays immutable; export applies saved overrides once. (Sources: `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialCore.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/spatial/SpatialObjectEdits.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialGraph.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientSpatialTools.js`, `webgpu-os/factory/apps/ambient-studio/AmbientImmersionControls.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientShaders.js`.)

Renderer version 1 grades the unpremultiplied scene radiance, then composites the premultiplied result with the saved background in linear light. It converts the background from sRGB and applies one sRGB transfer to the final color. Historical documents without that version retain their original display-space composition. Native pixel checks verify semitransparent captured splats over black and gray backgrounds and preserve the historical output in both core and compatibility mode. (Sources: `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientShaders.js`, `webgpu-os/kernel/drivers/SpatialAmbientLane.js`, `tests/ambient-spatial-rendering-native.test.js`, `artifacts/ambient-quality-review/immersive-final-linear-composition-native-20260930-r05.json`.)

### Prepare progressive detail for a static cloud

After importing a Gaussian cloud, open **Create â†’ Depth lab â†’ Build progressive detail**. Set pixel error, point count, resident memory and update timing, then choose **Build and enable**. Progressive detail supports static stored clouds with an explicit metric frame. It rejects motion sequences, source-projected media, linked depth or masks, and baked completion plates. Those sources retain their existing renderer. Importing replacement media, geometry, depth or motion clears obsolete progressive settings. This preparation partitions existing samples; it does not train new Gaussians, infer objects or restore records removed during import. The same values appear in **Project source Â· JSON** and the compiled spatial plan. | Saved streaming field | Default and meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `pixelError` | 2 pixels; smaller values request finer projected geometric detail, subject to budgets |
| `maxPoints` | 160,000; the effective limit also respects the source node's existing `count` |
| `maxResidentBytes` | 134,217,728 bytes (128 MiB); conservative reservation for source decoding, geometry, simulation and GPU staging |
| `maxConcurrentLoads` | 2; bounds simultaneous chunk resolutions |
| `settleMs` | 350 ms between eligible detail selections |
| `hysteresis` | 0.2; separates refinement and coarsening thresholds to reduce repeated switching |

A failed or cancelled replacement retains the visible selection. Reported resident bytes are reservations, not measured browser heap or total GPU memory; render-target textures remain under the compositor's pixel budget. The source project's asset count and export byte limits still apply.
